The Harionago Selvedge is a 14oz Japanese selvedge denim woven at low tension and left unsinged, resulting in a pronounced hairy surface texture. Made from 100% cotton and rope-dyed in indigo, the fabric embraces raw, expressive character and visible irregularity.
The denim draws its inspiration from the Japanese yōkai Harionago , a supernatural figure whose name translates to “Barbed-Hair Woman.” In Japanese folklore, Harionago is depicted as a beautiful but dangerous spirit who uses her long, thorn-like hair to ensnare and kill her victims. Her hair is often described as sharp, tangled, and inescapable; a visual metaphor echoed in the denim’s untamed, bristled surface.
This mythological reference is translated directly into material form. The unsinged fibers and rough texture mirror the creature’s wild hair, while custom artwork by Canadian artist Jacqui Oakley reinforces the narrative connection between folklore and fabric.

p-nakedandfamousdenim-14690191212909.d:
The MIJ16 Genseki Selvedge is a 19oz unsanforized Japanese selvedge denim developed for maximum texture and character. Genseki translates to “raw ore,” a term used to describe unrefined stone in its natural, extracted state. The name reflects the fabric perfectly. Dense, rough, and heavily textured, this denim feels raw and elemental. Woven using slubby and neppy yarns , the fabric displays an intense, irregular surface with visible neps throughout. This yarn character is amplified through low-tension weaving , allowing the fibers to relax and shift on the loom. An earthy-toned weft adds warmth beneath the indigo warp, enhancing contrast and depth as the denim ages.
To preserve the denim’s hairiness, rough texture, and unsanforized character, the MIJ16 undergoes a Tempi treatment . This process shrinks the fabric while maintaining its raw surface and structural integrity, removing guesswork from sizing while keeping the denim true to its original feel.
The selvedge edge features an indigo–red–indigo micro-busted line . The narrower selvedge width allows the warp color to extend closer to the edge, with a fine red line providing subtle contrast.

In our very early Wythe development, we knew we wanted to have a core bedford cord program - we had found so many vintage garments worn by cattlemen and ranchers in the 40s and 50s and the fabric spoke to us in a way that just felt right. These vintage pants were so broken in, so soft, yet still managed to feel bulletproof. We loved how it broke in and new this was going to be a staple of ours.
This particular bedford cord is just what we were looking for in a workwear staple. It's woven on vintage selvedge loom by a Japanese mill that specializes in weaving this fabric, exactly like it used to be made in the 40s and 50s. It's one of the only fabrics this mill produces.
One of the amazing things about bedford cord is how hard wearing it is on the outside, but how soft and stretchy it is on the inside. It breaks in and molds to your body like raw denim, and is easy to see why this was a favored fabric for workwear.
Our bedford cord has made its way onto what we call the "workwear straight leg". We're very stoked to be able to offer this fabric in multiple pant fits - a little somethin for everyone.
